title: Beyond plain water: Nanofluid‐wetted evaporative pre‐cooling for enhanced COP and reduced exergy destruction in split‐type air conditioners
content:
Abstract

This paper presents, for the first time, a coupled numerical–experimental investigation evaluating three metal-oxide nanofluids (TiO2/water, Al2O3/water and SiO2/water with volumetric concentrations of 0.1, 0.3 and 0.5 vol.%) as wetting media across three evaporative media pad geometries (corrugated, mesh-type, porous foam) applied to a 1.5-ton split-type air conditioner in a multi-variable parametric space not previously reported. A validated three-dimensional CFD model (ANSYS Fluent, mixture multiphase, y+ ≤ 1) is developed and experimentally validated, representing the first such model for nanofluid-wetted pre-cooling pads. Critically, this is also the first study to perform a component-level exergy analysis of a nanofluid-augmented evaporative pre-cooling system integrated with a vapor-compression cycle. Results show that Al2O3/water (0.5 vol.%) with the porous foam pad achieves a COP improvement of 30.5% at T amb = 45°C and RH = 30% improvement over the best plain-water benchmark (11%) reported in the literature. Second-law efficiency improved by 6.2 percentage points and condenser exergy destruction was reduced by 31%. The validated CFD model deviates from experiment by no more than ±3.1%, providing a design tool for optimization across the full MENA climatic envelope (T amb = 30–50°C, RH = 10–60%).
